A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching proofs and experiments across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 reports original neural-network experiments and fitted learning curves on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, and California Housing Prices.

after.justification: v2 Section 5 reports original experiments on the same four datasets, including numerical curve-fit results and an additional large-sample MNIST analysis.

M1.justification: The constrained ReLU network family, training losses, and SLSQP procedure for fitting the two rate curves remain unchanged. Adam is newly disclosed as the training optimizer; the PDFs do not establish an optimizer change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR10 and regression on California Housing Prices. The additional MNIST sample-size range changes the evaluation setting without adding a dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the same two fitted rate models, c1 + alpha/sqrt(n) and c2 + beta/n. No competing learning algorithm is added or replaced; the network architectures serve as experimental configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds MSE and R-squared for evaluating curve fits and a MNIST analysis starting at 20,000 training samples. It removes the MNIST CNN configuration while retaining the other architectures, dataset splits, sample-size increments, and SLSQP fitting procedure.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds a focused comparison of the two rate fits using larger MNIST training samples for shallow and four-hidden-layer networks. This supplements the full-range analysis by examining whether the comparison persists after excluding small-sample settings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 Appendix C.2 describes random training-subset selection, but does not establish replication at fixed settings or an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands quantitative reporting with four new tables of curve-fit MSE and R-squared across all four datasets. For example, Table 1 reports shallow-MNIST MSE of 0.017 for the 1/n curve versus 0.00052 for the 1/sqrt(n) curve. Large-sample MNIST results are added and MNIST CNN results removed; the overall reported preference for 1/sqrt(n) remains unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.2 specializes c from sqrt(tau*sigma/(40*kappa)) to sqrt(tau*sigma/160), using kappa = 4. Section 4 corrects mixture normalization and numerical factors, while Appendix A adds an explicit local-entropy definition and global/local entropy relation. These refine the existing argument without changing its central rate, assumptions, or packing construction.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the 1/sqrt(n) risk scaling, the corresponding 1/epsilon^4 sample requirement, and the novel packing-number lower bound. v2 promotes the entropy contribution into the abstract, but v1 already claims it in the introduction.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly notes that the bound does not determine an exact sample requirement in advance and explains that noisier data require more samples. It also interprets the fitted offsets as approximation error and clarifies conditional Gaussianity in the KL calculation.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.2 substantially expands implementation documentation beyond v1's losses and broad software descriptions. It discloses Adam, dataset-import and random-subset procedures, Colab/Deepnote execution, RAM and CPU specifications, and approximately eight hours of CIFAR10 computation. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Taheri et al. (2022), Friedman et al. (2010), Lemhadri et al. (2021), and Birge (1983), supporting generalization, sparsity, and local-packing discussions. The main positioning is retained; the updated Layer Sparsity reference represents the same work.

P1.justification: The lengthy packing-number proof moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix B.1, substantially streamlining the main narrative. The appendices are reorganized, the separate high-level proof outline is removed, and the empirical discussion is restructured around numerical comparisons and two MNIST sample ranges.

P2.justification: v2 adds four result tables and a two-panel large-sample MNIST figure, removes the MNIST CNN panel, and reformats the retained plots and captions. Figures are redistributed alongside the empirical discussion, replacing v1's presentation dominated by standalone plots.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the empirical evidence easier to assess through Tables 1–4 and the large-sample MNIST check, while Appendix C.2 improves implementation transparency. More explicit proof details and the reorganized narrative also help. The missing uncertainty reporting and loss of the MNIST CNN result limit these gains, supporting a modest overall improvement.
